panels.title: Uptime checks passing, by host
panels.description: Share of checker regions passing, by host. @@E@@Each check reads `/health` on a public host (the portal, auth and api hosts) from three US regions: a pass is the service answering through the load balancer and Cloud Armor. An outage pages when more than one region fails.@@Beta's hosts are behind IAP, so a check passes only on Google's sign-in page: it proves the address, the certificate, Cloud Armor and IAP, never the service behind them (that is the 5xx and instance panels). An outage pages when more than one region fails.@@

panels.title: IAP assertions refused, and stale pinned keys
panels.description: auth's or tpa-api's refusals of an IAP assertion under a key the image does not pin (urgent `iap-unknown-key`: most likely Google rotated IAP's keys), and the image's own warning that its keys are stale. Silent while beta runs with the header check off (R302).

panels.title: Requests, by service and status class
panels.description: Requests Cloud Run answered per interval.

panels.title: 5xx, by service
panels.description: 5xx answers per interval. `canary-5xx` opens above 0.1% of a service's requests over five minutes (and five); `backend-down` (urgent) when everything web, auth or tpa-api answered for ten minutes was a 5xx.

panels.title: p95 latency, by service (Cloud Run)
panels.description: Cloud Run's p95 request latency. web and tpa-api relay the desk's event streams, held open about 40 s by design, so theirs climbs whenever a desk page is open; beta's `canary-latency` leaves both out. tpa-api's real latency is the next panel.

panels.title: tpa-api p50 and p95 (its own request line)
panels.description: Time to the first byte from tpa-api's request line, without the live lane, the Ask lanes, uploads, downloads and the model-backed document rows (`tpa_api_latency`). `tpa-api-latency` opens above 2 s for ten minutes.

panels.title: tpa-api calls, by operation and outcome
panels.description: tpa-api's request lines in the time range, by the operation the route called, its outcome and status class (`tpa_api_requests`). Never the filled path, the tenant or the session.

panels.title: tpa-api outcomes
panels.description: tpa-api's request lines per interval, by outcome.

panels.title: Model gateway: vendor answers that failed, by kind
panels.description: model-gateway's calls to the model vendor that came back as an error, busy, unavailable or rejected (`model_gateway_calls`; `model-vendor-errors`). Silent while model-gateway is not built.

panels.title: Resources: each Cloud Run service's CPU, memory, instances, concurrency and start-up (open a row)
No disk on a Cloud Run service

options.content: **Cloud Run services have no disk.** A file a container writes is held in its memory, so a service's "disk space" is its **Memory** chart: files that grow show as memory climbing to the red line, then as a container killed for memory. Real disk is on the databases (each one's disk space is on its area's page and on Databases) and in the buckets. A **red line** is the line the pager uses (tpa-platform's alert policies); a **grey line** is a limit the service is set to.

panels.title: Resources · web: CPU, memory, instances, concurrency, start-up
CPU (p99, p95, p50)
panels.description: web's container CPU, the share of its CPU limit in use (`container/cpu/utilizations`): the 99th, 95th and 50th percentile across its instances in each 5-minute window. The red line is `run-cpu-high`'s: the p99 above 90% for 15 minutes pages (instances saturated: requests queue and slow).

links.title: web: CPU, memory, instances, concurrency, start-up

panels.title: Memory (p99, p95, p50)
panels.description: web's container memory, the share of its memory limit in use (`container/memory/utilizations`), percentiles across its instances in each 5-minute window. Cloud Run has no disk: files the container writes are held in memory and count here. The red line is `run-memory-high`'s: the p99 above 90% for 10 minutes pages; at the limit the container is killed (`run-oom`, the last panel of this row).

panels.title: Instances (total, active, idle)
panels.description: web's Cloud Run instances: the total, the most in each minute summed over active and idle, as the `ceiling-` policies read it, and active (serving or starting) and idle (kept warm, or waiting to be shut down) apart. max_instances is Cloud Run's default, 100, so the project's regional quota of 85 binds first (`run-instances-near-quota`: the project's instances, on its area's page).

panels.title: Concurrent requests, busiest instance (p99, p50)
panels.description: The most requests one instance served at once (`container/max_request_concurrencies`), its 99th and 50th percentile in each 5-minute window. The red line is `run-concurrency-high`'s: the p99 above 71.5 for 15 minutes pages. The grey line is the concurrency setting, 80: past it a request waits for a slot or a new instance.

panels.title: Start-up time (p99, p50)
panels.description: How long a new instance took to start, until it was ready to serve (`container/startup_latencies`): a dot for each interval in which one started. Nothing drawn: no instance started. No policy reads it; a start-up that failed is the last panel.

panels.title: Instances billed
panels.description: Billable instance time per second (`container/billable_instance_time`): how many instances were billed on average. An instance kept warm with CPU always on bills all the time; one that scales to zero, only while it serves.

panels.title: Killed for memory, crashed, failed to start
panels.description: From Cloud Run's own system log: a container killed for exceeding its memory limit (`run_oom_kills`; `run-oom` pages on one), a container that exited with an error or a signal (`run_crash_exits`; `run-crash-loop` at three in fifteen minutes), and a failed start-up or liveness probe (`run_system_errors`; `canary-startup`).

panels.title: The app project: instances against the regional quota, and egress through Cloud NAT (app-net-nat)
Cloud Run instances, every service
panels.description: Every Cloud Run instance in the app project, summed. The red line is `run-instances-near-quota`'s: above 68 for 10 minutes pages. The grey line is the regional quota, 85: at it no service can start another instance, whatever its own ceiling.

panels.title: NAT ports: allocated, and the most in use
panels.description: Cloud NAT's ports for auth's messenger, the model gateway and the synthetic journeys: the ports allocated to every instance behind the gateway (`nat/allocated_ports`), and the most connections one instance held to one destination (`nat/port_usage`). In use close to an instance's share of the allocated ports, new connections wait or drop. A cold gateway allocates ports as instances arrive, so the first calls after a quiet spell can wait.

panels.title: NAT new connections
panels.description: New connections Cloud NAT opened for auth's messenger, the model gateway and the synthetic journeys (`nat/new_connections_count`), per interval.

panels.title: NAT dropped packets
panels.description: Packets Cloud NAT dropped in each 5 minutes. Sent, out of ports: an outgoing packet with no port to leave by; the red line is `nat-port-exhaustion`'s, above 10 for 5 minutes. Sent, endpoint conflict: two instances reaching one destination from the same port. Received: replies with no open mapping (a connection already closed); a few are normal.

panels.title: NAT could not allocate
panels.description: Minutes in each 5 in which Cloud NAT could not allocate an address or ports (`nat/nat_allocation_failed`). The red line is `nat-port-exhaustion`'s: above 2 pages.

panels.title: Instances, by service
panels.description: Cloud Run instances per service (the most in each interval). A warm service with none pages as `no instance` (urgent).

panels.title: Start-up or runtime failures, and database proxy refusals
panels.description: Cloud Run's system log at ERROR (a failed probe, an exit, a memory limit: `canary-startup`) and the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy's refusals (`canary-sql`), for these services.

panels.title: Run summaries, by job
panels.description: One per scheduled run and per drain tick (`tpa_jobs_runs`). A drain that stops writing them has stopped.

panels.title: Alerts raised by runs
panels.description: Alert records the runs raised in the time range, by job and the registry's alert name (`jobs-alerts`; `anomaly_freeze`, `crm_signature_failure` and `member_access_mass_end` page as urgent). The record's tenant and detail are never read.

panels.title: Drain ticks that raised
panels.description: A tick of tpa-jobs-drains that raised instead of finishing (`drain-raised`), by drain and exception class. The loop keeps ticking and delivers nothing until it is fixed.
